evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/api/ApiClient.kt:63,85,107,137,163,188 — every suspend network method wraps the Ktor call in `catch (e: Exception) { Result.failure(e) }`. Because kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException IS an Exception, this SWALLOWS cooperative cancellation: when the enclosing scope is cancelled (e.g. the Compose `rememberCoroutineScope()` the ViewModels launch into is disposed as the screen leaves composition), the CancellationException is caught, converted to a Result.failure, and the coroutine body keeps running past the suspension point instead of unwinding — breaking structured concurrency.

Same anti-pattern is repeated in 8 more commonMain files: FavoritesRepository.kt (13 catch sites: getFavorites/addFavorite/removeFavorite/isFavorite/saved-search + alert methods), ListingRepository.kt, InquiryRepository.kt, NotificationRepository.kt, PortalListingsRepository.kt, RealtorRepository.kt, AgencyRepository.kt, and auth/SsoService.kt. grep: `grep -rn 'catch (e: Exception)' shared/src/commonMain` returns 58 sites; none except LayoutRepository rethrow CancellationException.

Proof the team already knows the correct fix and applied it in exactly ONE repo: LayoutRepository.kt:65 does `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` BEFORE the generic `catch (e: Exception)` (doc comment line 33: 'CancellationException is NOT swallowed — coroutine cancellation ...'), with a regression test at LayoutRepositoryTest.kt:266-270 asserting `assertFailsWith<CancellationException>`. The other 9 files never got the guard.

Concrete user-visible blast radius: SsoService.validateAndLogin (SsoService.kt:81-84) and loginWithPassword (SsoService.kt:180-183) catch the cancellation and set `_authState.value = AuthState.Error(e.message)` — a merely-cancelled auth flow (user backs out, config change) surfaces a spurious 'error' auth state. In ListingDetailViewModel.loadListing the swallowed cancellation flows into `.fold(onFailure = { errorMapper(e) })` and writes a phantom error message onto a screen that is being torn down. Fix: add `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` ahead of the generic catch in all 9 files (mirror LayoutRepository), or extract a shared `runCatchingApi {}` helper that rethrows CancellationException.
grep -rn 'CancellationException' shared/src/commonMain -> only LayoutRepository.kt imports/handles it; ApiClient + FavoritesRepository + SsoService + 6 others do not.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/api/HttpClientProvider.kt:37-43 — the single shared Ktor HttpClient installs ContentNegotiation, Logging(NONE), and a defaultRequest content-type, but NO `install(HttpTimeout)`. There is no requestTimeoutMillis, connectTimeoutMillis, or socketTimeoutMillis anywhere in the module (grep -rn 'HttpTimeout\|requestTimeoutMillis\|Timeout' shared/src returns nothing).

Impact on mobile: on a stalled/half-open connection (common on cellular handoff / captive portals) every repository suspend call — getListingDetail, favorites toggle, SSO validateAndLogin — hangs indefinitely with no upstream deadline. The UI state-holders flip isLoading=true and never receive a terminal onSuccess/onFailure, so the Compose CircularProgressIndicator (e.g. ListingDetailScreen.kt:116-119) spins forever with no error path and no retry affordance. This compounds the CancellationException-swallow finding: the only escape (scope cancellation) is itself swallowed by the repos.

Ktor default is NO timeout when the HttpTimeout plugin is not installed. Fix: `install(HttpTimeout) { requestTimeoutMillis = 30_000; connectTimeoutMillis = 15_000; socketTimeoutMillis = 30_000 }` in HttpClientProvider (applies uniformly to android ktor-client-android and iOS ktor-client-darwin engines since it is configured on the common client).

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoService.kt is a 349-line security-critical auth service (validateAndLogin, createMobileToken, loginWithPassword, register, requestPasswordReset/confirm, getSession, refreshSession, restoreSession, updateProfile, logout) with NO dedicated unit test. find shared/src/commonTest -name '*.kt' shows SsoStateStoreTest and SsoInitiationTest (which cover only the CSRF-nonce store/initiation), but no SsoServiceTest — none of the token-validation, login, or session-restore success/failure/authState transitions are exercised.

Every other repository/service in commonMain has behavioural coverage (LayoutRepositoryTest, NotificationRepositoryTest, FavoritesRepositoryTest, PortalListingsRepositoryTest, ProfileStatsLoaderTest, ListingDetailViewModelTest, PriceTrackingViewModelTest, ...), making SsoService the sole untested state-mutating class — and it is the one that drives AuthState across the whole app.

Given the SSO CSRF contract called out in mobile-native/CLAUDE.md ('Both platforms MUST verify a per-flow state nonce'), the absence of tests asserting validateAndLogin's success->Authenticated / non-2xx->Error / exception->Error transitions (via a Ktor MockEngine, the pattern already used in LayoutRepositoryTest) is a real coverage gap on the highest-risk surface. Fix: add SsoServiceTest with MockEngine cases for validateAndLogin + loginWithPassword + restoreSession happy/error paths, and (paired with the cancellation finding) a CancellationException-propagation assertion.
